claims.text: The 2D compound (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 can be deposited as a uniformly distributed spray-coated nanoflake layer.
Applying the (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 coating to CoCrFeNi will trigger a shear-induced tribocatalytic reaction.
The tribocatalytic reaction will form a continuously regenerating lubricious tribolayer.
The adaptive coating will maintain low friction and reduced wear on CoCrFeNi from 25 °C to 800 °C.
The adaptive coating will remain effective under variable loads and in both ambient and inert environments.
Untreated CoCrFeNi exhibits increased friction and wear variability over a wide temperature range.
An adhesion-promoting interlayer will ensure long-term integrity of the nanoflake coating.
High contact pressure promotes flattening of the nanoflakes and formation of a distributed lubricating film along the wear track.
Sliding shear stress activates tribocatalytic behavior in the 2D HEA nanoflake coating.
The tribolayer may contain stable oxides or amorphous carbon compounds.
The proposed tribolayer minimizes surface adhesion.
The proposed tribolayer retards oxidation and suppresses plastic deformation.
The adhesion-promoting interlayer will stabilize the coating across the entire 25–800 °C range.
The coated CoCrFeNi will exhibit a coefficient of friction near 0.08–0.1 throughout the specified test range.
The coating will reduce the wear rate of CoCrFeNi by at least one order of magnitude relative to uncoated CoCrFeNi.
Friction and wear of untreated CoCrFeNi escalate with temperature and load.
The performance benefit will hold at contact pressures from 0.5 to 1.0 GPa in ambient or inert gas from 25 °C to 800 °C.
Efficacy may be limited above 800 °C or in chemically aggressive environments.
Prior evidence demonstrates low friction, low wear, and tribocatalytic self-lubricating behavior for (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 nanoflakes at room temperature and high contact pressure.
Long-term durability and adhesion under prolonged high-temperature and high-load operation remain uncertain.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and experimental design specify an adhesion-promoting interlayer, whereas the intervention permits either an interlayer or an optimized post-spray heat treatment. These are distinct implementations, so the intervention is not uniquely fixed.

The outcome claims performance consistently at every specified temperature, pressure, and environment, but the falsification rule requires failure across the entire range. Failure at even one in-boundary condition would contradict the universal prediction but would not necessarily satisfy the stated rule.
